title: Stroke-sculpt pipeline frictions from the blind skull runs

description:
Frictions the blind stroke-sculpt skull runs hit (MESH-72 run 1, MESH-75 run 2, MESH-79 run 3), collected so the stroke-sculpt pipeline stops making sculptors work around its tools. Each item names what happened; the evidence is in those tickets' changes-made and the sculptors' reports.

Stroke sculpting (StrokeSculpt, StrokeSketch, stroke_sculpt node):
1. Strokes near a silhouette silently do nothing. Since MESH-76 a stroke only touches surface its camera sees; a stroke within about 40 px of its cell's outline lands on surface seen edge-on and has no effect, with no warning. Only stroke-lift shows it, and only against a hand-built partial DSL. So an outline can never be moved from the view in which it is the outline. Report dropped strokes from the node, and give the sculptor a way to move a silhouette (for example a silhouette stroke that drags the outline itself).
2. 3D mirroring breaks on a surface that is no longer exactly symmetric. symmetry="x" and data-mirror put mirrored points slightly off the surface after any one-sided refinement, giving "ambiguous nearest vertex ... tie, move the point" errors (runs 2 and 3, about six times in run 3; a one-pixel nudge clears it, so a loading sculpt can break after an unrelated edit) and pits. The run-3 sculptor stopped using data-mirror and drew each mirrored stroke in the opposite cell instead.
3. Two large strokes in one pass leave pits on the far side of the head; each alone is clean (found by bisecting a layer). Workaround was one big push per layer.
4. Refinement grows without bound and leaves noise: run 3 went from a 4k-vertex base to 99k after round 4 and 166k after round 5 (load 3.5 s and rising, 2 GB heap), and the refined cranium shows streaky noise; broad data-op="smooth" strokes add streaks instead of removing them.
5. Fills give an even depth with a short edge falloff, so cavities come out flat-bottomed with stepped sides (eye sockets, nasal opening); the sculptor stacked two fills to fake a bowl.
6. Detail strokes lower chamfer but make the shaded form less faithful: run 3's image distance (1 - SSIM on clay renders vs the goal) rose from 0.271 at the base to 0.324 by round 4 while chamfer fell. Placement and shape of features (sockets, teeth, grooves) needs better tools than freehand polylines.

Base mesh (silhouette_hull, trace-outlines, trace-reference, quad_layout):
7. The strict hull sits inside every traced outline (rounding and smoothing shrink it further): run 3's base failed its silhouette checkpoint (sum 91 px vs 70, Back 23.6 px).
8. The hull of slightly inconsistent traces came out asymmetric: the base's face was turned, its right half up to 0.17 behind the left, for a symmetric subject. silhouette_hull or trace-outlines needs a symmetry option.
9. trace-reference fits each trace to the sculpt's own height in that cell, so a size shortfall can never show in a trace; traced silhouette strokes crumpled the forehead in run 3.
10. quad_layout still fails on hulls with less rounding or no smoothing ("map is folded"), so the base is pinned to one parameter set (see PATCH-127).

Workflow and CLI:
11. load_mesh resolves paths from the module directory while stroke_sculpt's svg= resolves from resources (dsl/...), so the same DSL needs two path styles.
12. Round snapshots need every svg= and load_mesh path rewritten to absolute by hand to evaluate elsewhere, and a snapshot holding base.dsl makes sculpt-animate --rounds refuse ("holds 2 .dsl files"). A snapshot command should write a self-contained round.
13. Inspecting a pass's input needs hand-made partial DSLs (mesh-dsl --name on a file DSL was unclear), and the sculptors keep writing the same scripts: outline overlap / diff / overdraw (run 2), depth probes by lifting a row of strokes and a stroke-lift summary (run 3). These should be ixdar-cli commands.

14. One pen size and one pen strength. Today size comes from stroke-width (view pixels, so its world size depends on the cell's lens and distance), r= in the strokes text (world), the node's falloff (edge-path distance, the default when neither is given); strength from data-strength (silently clamped to [-1, 1]), data-kind ridge/valley (overrides its sign), the node's strength (an unclamped multiplier on the whole layer; MESH-75's 2.0 turned the mesh inside out) and the node's scale (world distance per unit strength), plus a hidden per-point weight from how face-on the surface is. Make the stroke the one place a sculptor sets size (in world units, independent of lens) and strength (one value, no hidden clamp), and document in the stroke_sculpt node description exactly what sets the displacement, so a sculptor reading only the catalog knows what affects what.

15. Sculptors learn what a stroke does by trial and error (stroke-lift, depth probes, bisecting layers). Make it readable instead: for every stroke, the node (and an ixdar-cli command over a DSL and a layer name) reports its effective world radius, its peak displacement after every multiplier, how many points lifted, and how many were dropped and why (grazing, off-surface, out of cell). The stroke_sculpt catalog description states the formula from SVG attributes to displacement, so the skill can point at it instead of restating it.

16. A stroke on the mirror plane with data-mirror runs twice on itself and leaves a dent (run 3 round 9, the upper back); the node should skip or merge a mirror copy that overlaps its original, or warn.

17. The saved base has a pinch at the upper left of the dome seen from behind, where some faces point inward (run 3 round 13; it shows in the base's own capture). Sculpt strokes cannot remove it: smoothing barely softens it and a push puckers it. Find which base stage (volume_to_mesh, keep_largest_part, smooth_mesh, quad_layout) leaves inward faces and stop it there; the base must have no folded faces before sculpting starts.
definition-of-done:
1. Every numbered friction in the description is fixed, or split into its own ticket (linked here with --blocks) with the reason it is bigger than this ticket.
2. Each fix names its cause in changes-made and is covered by a test, or by a before/after capture under tmp/ for the visual ones.
3. dsl/skull3/skull.dsl from MESH-79 still loads and looks the same, or the changes-made says what changed and why.
4. The stroke-sculpt skill (ai-workspace .claude/skills/stroke-sculpt/SKILL.md) is listed in the report where its advice is now stale; do not edit it.

No file under ixdar_automation_cli/ does geometry, camera, mesh or image maths (no cv2 or numpy for that); outline comparison, tracing, symmetry (as a silhouette_hull port), migration and height maths run in Java automation routes, including the tracing MESH-77 landed in trace_outlines and trace_reference.
testing-plan:
1. StrokeSculptTest and SilhouetteHullNodeTest.
2. Reproduce items 1-3 on the MESH-79 skull layers before and after.
3. Load dsl/skull3/skull.dsl and record load time and vertex count before and after.
changes-made: Item 1 (dropped strokes): cause, a stroke within about its width of a cell's outline lifts only onto surface seen edge-on (StrokeSketch drops points under cosine 0.25) or onto vertices its camera cannot see, and nothing said so. stroke_sculpt now has a report output: per stroke its kind, cell, radius, depth, points lifted and dropped (grazing, off-surface, out of cell), vertices moved and peak displacement, and DROPPED with the reason, pointing at a data-kind=silhouette stroke, which drags the outline itself, as the way to move an outline from its own view. Test: StrokeSculptTest.theReportNamesAStrokeOnTheOutlineAsDropped.

Item 2 (mirror ties): cause, StrokeSculpt picked mirror twins and stroke-sample normals with NearestVertex.find, which refuses a near tie (right for authored points), and averaged every vertex with its nearest mirror vertex even on a surface that is not exactly symmetric (a quad layout, an earlier one-sided pass), which blurs and pits. New NearestVertex.nearest(x, y, z, reach) takes any tied vertex; a vertex's twin is now only a vertex at its mirror image within a tenth of its shortest edge, and a vertex without one keeps its own displacement, which the reflected strokes already made symmetric. Tests: StrokeSculptTest.mirrorTwinsTolerateASurfaceThatIsNotQuiteSymmetric (tie refused by find, taken by nearest; a turned sphere's cheek keeps its full peak), symmetricPassMirrorsAOneSidedStroke still passes.

Item 16 (data-mirror on the mirror plane): cause, a stroke and its own reflection both ran as separate copies (only fills were joined). Any reflected copy whose every point lies within half the radius of an earlier copy of the same stroke is now dropped. Test: StrokeSculptTest.aMirroredStrokeOnTheMirrorPlaneRunsOnce (fails with the check disabled).
Item 3 (two large strokes pit the far side): not reproducible without MESH-79's layers, which are not on master while that blind run is live; split to MESH-81 with the candidate causes.

Item 4 (refinement growth and streaks): cause of the part fixed here, smooth strokes refined to a third of their width though smoothing adds no detail, and the umbrella smoothing then wrote the new transition faces into the surface as streaks; smooth strokes no longer refine or shrink their neighbours' refinement gap. Test: StrokeSculptTest.aSmoothStrokeDoesNotRefine. Growth is now visible per layer (report line 'N vertices in, M after refinement'; stroke-report). The unbounded growth across layers (nothing ever coarsens) needs a coarsening design: split to MESH-82.

Item 5 (flat-bottomed fills): cause, a fill's kernel is the union of its samples' bumps, which saturates to a flat floor with only an r-wide rim. A fill's kernel is now that union times the bump-weighted mean of its samples' weights, and data-profile="bowl" on a polygon weights each sample t(2 - t) by its distance in from the outline over the deepest sample's, so the floor curves up to the rim. Unweighted fills are unchanged. Test: StrokeSculptTest.aBowlFillCurvesItsFloorUpToTheRim (near the rim the bowl sinks 0.051 where the flat fill sinks 0.149, same centre depth).
Item 6 (feature placement tools): a tool design, not a defect; split to MESH-83.

Item 7 (hull inside every outline): measured with the new outline-compare: rounding and smoothing cost under 10 of the 86 px seven-view sum; the raw strict hull at resolution 96 still sums 69.6 (Back 20.6). Cause: the strict intersection of traces that disagree, chiefly the Back picture's scale. Split to MESH-84 (consistent trace fitting or a probabilistic silhouette term), with the numbers.

Item 8 (asymmetric hull): cause, each picture's trace is placed independently, so a symmetric subject's left and right traces disagree and the strict hull takes the tighter of each pair. trace-outlines --symmetry x averages each outline's signed distance with its mirror's (front, back, top with their own flip; right with left; the two 3/4 cells with each other). On dsl/silhouette_hull_skull's traces the hull's mirror distance fell from mean 0.047 / max 0.254 to 0.011 / 0.038 and its outline-compare sum against the traces from 84.1 to 67.0 px (tmp/mesh-80-measurements.json).

Item 9 (trace-reference fitted to the sculpt): cause, the trace was scaled to the sculpt's own silhouette height, so a size shortfall could never show. trace-reference --height H scales it to the subject's world height at the cell's orbit target instead; its silhouettes now carry data-radius (world) instead of data-strength/stroke-width (--radius).
Item 10 (quad_layout folding on hulls): PATCH-127's, unchanged here.

Item 11 (two path styles): cause, load_mesh resolved through MeshLoader.resolve (working directory, ixdar-app) and stroke_sculpt's svg through its own list (plus src/main/resources). MeshLoader.resolve now tries src/main/resources with and without the module, and StrokeSketch.read uses it, so one path (dsl/<subject>/base.ply) works for both. Test: StrokeSculptTest.loadMeshAndSvgResolveOneResourcePath.

Item 12 (round snapshots): new ixdar-cli sculpt-snapshot copies the sculpt DSL and every file its nodes read (stroke_sculpt and silhouette_hull svg, load_mesh path) into the next tmp/rounds/round<NN>/ and points the copy at those files by absolute path; sculpt-animate --rounds now takes the one DSL with stroke_sculpt layers and ignores a base.dsl beside it. Checked: run-2 skull snapshot with a base.dsl added animates (tmp/animate-test/).

Item 13 (inspection scripts): mesh-dsl --name now takes a .dsl file path relative to the checkout (it only took packaged names or absolute paths) and documents --node for a layer's input; new ixdar-cli stroke-report (every layer's per-stroke report for a DSL), outline-compare (per cell IoU, mean/max px, short/over area and an overlay against an outlines template, the run-2 iou/diff/overdraw scripts and run-3's checkpoint; reproduces MESH-79's checkpoint numbers: Front 11.4, Back 22.8, sum 86); stroke-lift rows now carry kind, depth, outOfCell. Depth probes: stroke-lift's stroke text lists every lifted point.

Item 14 (one size, one strength): causes, five sources of size and strength. Now the stroke alone sets both in world units: SVG data-radius (falloff radius; silhouettes: reach) and data-depth (signed displacement at the stroke), no clamp; data-strength is refused with the migration hint, ridge/valley only label the sign (a contradiction is refused), stroke-width is only drawn, the hidden face-on weight is gone, silhouettes drag fully onto the stroke, and the node's strength, scale and falloff ports are removed (crease stays, one weight per chain). The strokes text is 'd r=R ...' in world units with r required. The node description states the formula. New ixdar-cli sculpt-migrate converts a DSL and its SVGs, measuring each width where the old lift did (on the layer's input). Samples migrated: stroke_sculpt_head (+ its three SVGs), stroke_sculpt_sphere, stroke_crease_sphere; their captures match master within RMSE 1.7 (tmp/captures/before vs after2). The live tool still takes view-pixel width and depth over width and writes world values.

Item 15 (what a stroke does): the report output and ixdar-cli stroke-report give each stroke's world radius, depth, peak displacement after everything, points lifted and dropped by reason (grazing, off-surface, out of cell); the catalog description gives the formula from attributes to displacement.

Item 17 (inward faces on skull3/base.ply): stage found by exporting each stage and counting faces folded against their corners' summed normals: volume_to_mesh, keep_largest_part and smooth_mesh 0, quad_layout 20 of 8,134 (the pinch at the upper back among them). quad_layout makes them from a fold-free input; split to PATCH-128 (quad-layout pipeline, out of this ticket's scope).

DoD 3 (skull3 still loads): not checkable here while MESH-79's skull.dsl is unlanded. Its SVGs use data-strength and must be converted with ixdar-cli sculpt-migrate --dsl dsl/skull3/skull.dsl (scene running) when it lands; expected differences, shown on the archived run-2 skull (tmp/captures/before vs after2 skull75): silhouettes at node strength above 1 now drag exactly onto their stroke, and ridges on oblique surface lose the old hidden face-on fade. Run-2 skull: 196,788 to 131,224 vertices, 2.29 s to 1.14 s. Follow-up for the 810-line StrokeSculpt.apply (7,973 of HotSpot's 8,000 bytecode bytes, MESH-78 adds more): MESH-85.

Moved to Java (the user's rule in Ixdar/CLAUDE.md '# Automation': the Python CLI does no geometry, camera, mesh or image maths). trace-reference, trace-outlines and outline-compare are now routes (mesh/trace-reference, mesh/trace-outlines, ui/outline-compare) whose generated CLI commands keep the old flags and output shape; their Python files and OpenCV/numpy are gone. The maths lives in reusable classes: SubjectOutline (picture decode via the platform, border-median background, largest blob's contour from PixelImage.outlines' Moore tracing, interior edges), PolylineSimplify (Douglas-Peucker, now also PixelImage.outlines'), ReferenceOutlines (Camera3D cell axes, the log-space shared-scale fit, the oblique fit to the carved lattice hull), DistanceTransform (exact Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher EDT) and OutlineOverlap (IoU, morphological-gradient boundary distances, short/over). multiview takes --camera <svg> to capture through a template's camera, which outline-compare and sculpt-animate use instead of Python framing maths; stroke-lift rows carry strokeWidthRadius (Camera3D.worldPerPixel at the lifted points, at the target for silhouettes), which sculpt-migrate reads instead of computing it. Item 8's symmetry is now silhouette_hull's symmetry="x" port, applied to the voxel volume: a lattice point is kept by the mean of its own and its mirror image's signed depth inside the deciding view's outline (exactly the old vote when unmirrored); trace-outlines --symmetry is dropped. On silhouette_hull_skull: hull mirror distance mean 0.047 / max 0.254 -> 0.010 / 0.044. Checks: outline-compare via the route on the MESH-79 checkpoint traces gives sum 86.2 px, Back 22.9 (Python gave 86.0 / 22.8); route-backed sculpt-migrate reproduces the earlier radii exactly; trace-outlines and trace-reference smoke-tested on cropped captures (tmp/refs/). Tests: unit.automation.OutlineTracingTest (outline IoU and distance on a hand-made pair, contour of a synthetic ellipse, ellipsoid pictures at unrelated zooms fitted to one scale, ported from test_cli's cv2 tests, which are removed), SilhouetteHullNodeTest.symmetryXEvensOutALopsidedTrace. grep for cv2/numpy imports under ixdar_automation_cli: none. Left: quilt_mesh_fingerprint.py still does mesh maths in Python (pre-existing, not touched); MultiviewScreenshot's handler is now about 307 lines (was 297).
review-summary: Stroke sculpt strokes now set their own size and depth in world units, and every stroke_sculpt layer reports what each stroke did, dropped ones named. The blind skull runs kept working around silent, mismatched and unscriptable sculpt tools; the rest are fixed or split into tickets.
